persona: everyday customer: a coastal traveller who collects lighthouses

designs.title: Fanad Head Lighthouse
designs.why: Instantly recognisable: white tower, keepers' cottages and the cliff over Lough Swilly are right, and the facts check out (first lit 17 March 1817, 1886 tower, 22 m, correct coordinates). The info blocks read cleanly and the arched title looks like a real souvenir poster. Up close the 'engraving' is more traced outline than true hatching, and the lower third of rock goes into a heavy dark mass.
designs.fix: Thin out the dark rocks and sea in the bottom third with more open hatching so the cliff reads as engraved texture instead of a black blot on the chest.

designs.title: Portland Head Light
designs.why: The most-visited lighthouse in the set and it looks the part: keeper's house, tall tower and Cape Elizabeth ledges, with accurate dates (1787-1790, first lit 10 January 1791) and coordinates. But the right-hand 'HISTORIC SITE / U.S. NATIONAL REGISTER' note reads awkwardly, the house and rocks fill the lower half so densely that the tower gets lost on the black tee, and the coordinate quote marks look different from the other prints.
designs.fix: Change the right block to 'NATIONAL REGISTER OF HISTORIC PLACES' (or the 1791 lighting note), and lighten the foreground rocks so the white tower stands out.

designs.title: Cape Agulhas Lighthouse
designs.why: The banded tower with its flanking pylons is unmistakably Agulhas, the southern tip of Africa, a place a collector is proud to have been. It is the cleanest layout of the four: a big readable title, a short fact block (built 1848, first lit 1849) and correct S/E coordinates. Plenty of air around the tower, so it holds up best from across a room. The facts feel a little thin next to the others.
designs.fix: Add one line a traveller cares about, e.g. 'SOUTHERNMOST TIP OF AFRICA' or 'WHERE TWO OCEANS MEET', under the coordinates to balance the left block.

designs.title: Phare de Saint-Mathieu
designs.why: My favourite: the abbey ruins beside the tower are exactly why people go to Saint-Mathieu, and here they are, with a proper French heading and 'Plougonvelin, Finistère, Bretagne' (accents intact). The facts are right (1835, 37 m). The two-line title takes more vertical space and the bottom half of rocks and ruins is very dense, so on the shirt the lower part turns into a dark slab.
designs.fix: Open up the hatching on the foreground rocks and abbey walls so the ruins stay readable as stonework when printed at shirt size.
